knowledge:
- key_parameters: exprMatr=Matrix of gene expression data where rows are genes and columns are samples ;; regulators=Vector of candidate regulators (indices or names) or a list specifying candidate regulators for each target gene ;; targets=Vector of target genes to restrict the analysis ;; treeMethod=Tree-based method to use, either "RF" (Random Forest, default) or "ET" (Extra-Trees) ;; K=Number of candidate regulators randomly selected at each node ("sqrt", "all", or an integer) ;; nTrees=Number of trees grown per ensemble (default is 1000) ;; nCores=Number of cores to use for parallel execution ;; returnMatrix=Logical indicating whether to return a weight matrix (default TRUE) or a list (required FALSE when regulators is a list) ;; reportMax=Maximum number of top-ranked links to report in getLinkList ;; threshold=Weight threshold to filter links in getLinkList
- alternatives: treeMethod="RF" (Random Forest, default) vs treeMethod="ET" (Extra-Trees, which is faster and can be more randomized)
- when_to_use: When you want to infer directed gene regulatory networks and rank regulatory links from steady-state transcriptomics/gene expression data (microarray, RNA-seq, etc.).
- pitfalls: The weights of the links returned by GENIE3 do not have statistical meaning and only provide a ranking, meaning there is no standard threshold value. Normalization, filtering, and log-transformation of the input expression matrix will affect the results. set.seed ensures reproducibility, but results may differ between nCores=1 and nCores>1. The ranking of links varies slightly between runs due to the intrinsic randomness of the tree methods; increase nTrees to reduce this variance.

workflows.name: standard_network_inference
workflows.intent: Infer a gene regulatory network from a gene expression matrix using default or customized tree-based parameters and extract ranked regulatory links.
input: exprMatr (matrix of gene expression data where rows are genes and columns are samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare the gene expression matrix ;; 2. Run GENIE3 to compute regulatory link weights (optionally customizing tree method, parameters, or parallelization) ;; 3. Extract and filter the ranked list of regulatory links.
workflows.code:
exprMatr <- matrix(sample(1:10, 100, replace=TRUE), nrow=20)
rownames(exprMatr) <- paste("Gene", 1:20, sep="")
colnames(exprMatr) <- paste("Sample", 1:5, sep="")
library(GENIE3)
set.seed(123) # For reproducibility of results
weightMat <- GENIE3(exprMatr)
weightMat <- GENIE3(exprMatr, treeMethod="ET", K=7, nTrees=50)
weightMat <- GENIE3(exprMatr, nCores=4, verbose=TRUE)
linkList <- getLinkList(weightMat)
linkList <- getLinkList(weightMat, reportMax=5)
linkList <- getLinkList(weightMat, threshold=0.1)

workflows.name: targeted_network_inference
workflows.intent: Infer a gene regulatory network while restricting the candidate regulators to a specific subset of genes or defining target-specific regulator sets.
input: exprMatr (matrix of gene expression data where rows are genes and columns are samples)
regulators (vector of candidate regulator gene names/indices or a list mapping target genes to their potential regulators)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare the gene expression matrix and define the candidate regulators ;; 2. Run GENIE3 with the restricted regulator set (globally or per-target) ;; 3. Extract the resulting regulatory links.
workflows.code:
exprMatr <- matrix(sample(1:10, 100, replace=TRUE), nrow=20)
rownames(exprMatr) <- paste("Gene", 1:20, sep="")
colnames(exprMatr) <- paste("Sample", 1:5, sep="")
library(GENIE3)
regulators <- c("Gene2", "Gene4", "Gene7")
weightMat <- GENIE3(exprMatr, regulators=regulators)
regulatorsList <- list("Gene1"=rownames(exprMatr)[1:10],
                       "Gene2"=rownames(exprMatr)[10:20],
                       "Gene20"=rownames(exprMatr)[15:20])
set.seed(123)
weightList <- GENIE3(exprMatr, nCores=1, targets=names(regulatorsList), regulators=regulatorsList, returnMatrix=FALSE)
